lore: At every dusk the keeper presses a shell into the wet sand of each save, a perfect print of the island as it stood. A new shell only needs fresh sand where a save has changed; everything else it borrows from the shells before it. When a villager wrecks a save and begs for the island as it was last week, the keeper finds the right shell and pours it back. Keep every shell and the beach fills up; keep too few and last week is gone.

lines.start: Twelve hundred saves and forty dusks. One shell a night, and only fresh sand where something changed.
lines.press: Pressed. Most of this shell is borrowed from yesterday's.
lines.restore: Last week, you said? Here's the shell. Pour it back and it's exactly as it was.
lines.win: Every shell anyone asked for came back perfect, and the beach never overflowed.
lines.fail: Either the beach is buried in shells or the one they wanted is gone. Rethink how many you keep.
